segments.text: On the twenty-second of June, nineteen forty-one, at zero three fifteen in the morning, Germany invaded the Soviet Union. Operation Barbarossa had begun.
Three million German soldiers stood on the Soviet frontier, backed by three thousand tanks, and six hundred thousand horses.
In a single day, the Soviet Air Force lost one thousand eight hundred and eleven aircraft. Nearly one thousand five hundred were destroyed on the ground, before they ever took off.

By the end of nineteen forty-one, the great encirclements had swallowed whole armies. Minsk: three hundred twenty thousand prisoners. Smolensk: three hundred thousand. Kiev: six hundred sixty-five thousand.
By November, Germany occupied sixty-three percent of Soviet coal, fifty-eight percent of steel, and forty percent of grain.
